items.markdown:
Comprehensible input (CI) is a language acquisition method based on Stephen Krashen's theory that people learn a language best by **understanding messages in context** rather than memorizing grammar rules or vocabulary lists.[[1]](https://freehebrew.online/why-our-method/)[[2]](https://cmovan.edublogs.org/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qGr2o7xycnk)

You can find curated resources, video channels, and structured platforms dedicated to Hebrew comprehensible input:

### Top Modern Hebrew Comprehensible Input Sources

- **Reelang Hebrew:** A TikTok-style video feed with content filterable by level (A1 to C1), topic, and listening speed (slow, medium, fast).
- **Piece of Hebrew:** Engages learners with vlogs and lifestyle content about Israel with low-intermediate to intermediate pacing.
- **Lenguia:** Offers short animated stories and beginner (A1) Hebrew videos with synchronized interactive transcripts where you can tap words to see meanings.
- **Free Hebrew. Forever:** A free online curriculum that uses a natural approach, delaying text and the alphabet in early lessons to mimic natural childhood acquisition.
- **Alisa Shapiro's Composable Hebrew Resources:** Educator blogs and teacher guides focused on big-idea, message-driven Modern Hebrew acquisition.
- **Wiki Directory:** You can browse a larger breakdown of tools on the [Comprehensible Input Wiki for Hebrew](https://comprehensibleinputwiki.org/wiki/Hebrew).[[1]](https://comprehensibleinputwiki.org/wiki/Hebrew)[[2]](https://www.lenguia.com/comprehensible-input/hebrew)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THaBh2-Xbys)[[4]](https://freehebrew.online/why-our-method/)[[5]](https://cmovan.edublogs.org/)

### A Note on Biblical vs. Modern Hebrew

- **Aleph with Beth:** An exceptionally popular and high-quality YouTube resource for CI, though it teaches **Biblical Hebrew** rather than Modern Hebrew. Because of heavy vocabulary overlap, some learners use it to bridge gaps, keep in mind that pronunciation, syntax, and daily usage differ from Modern Hebrew.[[1]](https://comprehensibleinputwiki.org/wiki/Hebrew)
